## Schedules, retransmission and wire connections

Service inquiries concern transmission periods, substitute stations and wire connections.

| Subject | Summary | Page editions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Eilvese listening and transmission periods** | The telegram specifies Eilvese sending and receiving arrangements and provisional transmission windows; numerical assignments and unstated units remain qualified. | [p113](../pages/113.md#source-p113-d1) |
| **NKJ backup and relay arrangements** | Repeated messages ask which station could replace NKJ during interruption and whether NKJ relays Mackensen traffic. Sevastopol is proposed as a backup. | [p190](../pages/190.md#source-p190-b) · [p193](../pages/193.md#source-p193-a) |
| **Wire communications and Braila–Tiraspol return instructions** | Related receptions discuss wire communications, instructions for the Ackermann post to return from Braila, and a Tiraspol continuation. | [p162](../pages/162.md#source-p162-c1) · [p166](../pages/166.md#source-p166-c1) |

## Cipher instructions and service procedure

Ringbahn instructions extend the use of November keys; the September orders regulate listening and acknowledgments.

| Subject | Summary | Page editions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **The Tiflis Ringbahn instruction** | The instruction retains November Ringbahn keys for December use, starting with the 10 November key on 1 December 1918. | [p146](../pages/146.md#source-p146-c1) |
| **Instructions to reuse Ringbahn keys** | November Ringbahn keys are to be retained and the December key postponed. The continuation schedules reuse through 21 December 1918. | [p160](../pages/160.md#source-p160-c1) |
| **September radio-service procedure** | Daily listening instructions accompany a separate request to send radiograms during reception of the Nauen press and postpone acknowledgments until afterward. | [p60](../pages/060.md#source-p60-a1) |

## Vehicles, equipment and departures

Departure arrangements combine vehicle allocation, equipment movement and continued station service.

| Subject | Summary | Page editions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Trucks, trailers, readiness and the Hanau destination** | Truck and trailer messages concern readiness, departure arrangements and Hanau as a destination. A truck-departure report says the sender plans to remain with a number of men until Sunday; timings remain incomplete. | [p185](../pages/185.md#source-p185-d) · [p189](../pages/189.md#source-p189-e) · [p193](../pages/193.md#source-p193-e) · [p194](../pages/194.md#source-p194-a) · [p196](../pages/196.md#source-p196-b) · [p197](../pages/197.md#source-p197-e) · [p198](../pages/198.md#source-p198-c) |
| **Loading apparatus and keeping the station ready** | Parallel orders send two US apparatuses toward Darmstadt while retaining station readiness, and select the best trailer for loading with a petrol pump held ready. | [p197](../pages/197.md#source-p197-c) · [p198](../pages/198.md#source-p198-b) |
| **Station control and Seifert’s arrival and departure messages** | Station reports describe soldiers’ council supervision, continued operation and custody of cipher keys. Separate messages concern Seifert’s movements and immediate listening instructions. | [p168](../pages/168.md#source-p168-a) · [p169](../pages/169.md#source-p169-a) · [p172](../pages/172.md#source-p172-a) · [p174](../pages/174.md#source-p174-b) |
| **Arrival, departure and car inquiries on 12 November 1918** | Short messages report arrival and departure, request notice when Seifert arrives, and ask where the car is. Repeated texts do not establish additional journeys. | [p183](../pages/183.md#source-p183-a) |
| **Postponed departure, supper inquiry and farewell** | Distinct service messages postpone a departure, ask for a headcount for a warm evening meal, and convey a farewell. | [p193](../pages/193.md#source-p193-c) · [p196](../pages/196.md#source-p196-a) |
